descriptor.scene: There is no human being in this frame and no second mascot figure. EXACTLY ONE mitten arm is in this picture and it belongs to the manager; there is NO second arm and NO disembodied limb anywhere in the image. THE CAMERA HAS WALKED IN CLOSE. This is the delivery, the one thing he ever leans out of the machine to do: the manager leans OUT through the open mouth of a honey-wood chute, his legs and the whole of his body staying inside it. He fills the UPPER LEFT of the frame from the chest up, his head about a third of the frame height, his cream newsboy cap level on his head, his dot eyes turned down toward the book, and ONE mitten arm reaching down out of the chute mouth to rest lightly on the book and steady it as it settles. That arm is in scale with his own small body and it is a smooth rounded stub with no fingers, no thumb and no hand. Filling the LOWER AND RIGHT of the frame, a finished picture book has slid out onto a smooth cream tray: closed, small, warmly bound in cloth with a plain cream cover, its pages crisp and new, with no lettering, no title, no words and no numbers anywhere on it. His plum light and the warm honeyed afternoon light from above fall together across the cover. Composition: chute mouth and manager upper left, book and tray filling the lower right; the upper right stays calm warm wall.
descriptor._caption: By afternoon the book slides out finished: painted, bound, and read aloud in a warm voice. June touched the beginning, when she said what was on her heart, and she will touch the end. The long middle belonged to the factory.
negatives: a second arm, a second mitten stub, or any limb that belongs to no visible body
a mitten stub larger than the book or out of scale with the manager's own body
fingers, a thumb, a hand or a glove on the mitten stub
the manager standing outside the machine with his legs out of the chute
a title, lettering or any readable mark on the book

The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. If a person in this scene is moving toward something, that destination MUST BE AHEAD OF THEM IN THE FRAME and they must be seen FROM BEHIND or from three-quarters behind, so the viewer is following them into it. A figure whose face is toward the camera is walking AWAY from everything behind them: if the thing they are moving toward is drawn behind them, the picture says the opposite of the scene. Their feet, hips, shoulders and gaze all point the same way, along the direction of travel. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
